w:r.w:t: Ascend Backend API Rebrand Change Description
Mobile integration impact and compatibility reference

The backend changes are customer-facing brand updates from Xenoh to Ascend. They do not add, remove, or rename API endpoints, HTTP methods, request fields, response schemas, authentication contracts, server URLs, or the API version. Mobile clients can keep their existing networking layer and models. They should update visible copy and expect Ascend wording in selected messages, emails, AI content, and generated share images.

This document compares the current Xenoh backend working tree with its current Git HEAD. It describes the tracked rebrand changes in API, Application, and Infrastructure code plus the checked-in OpenAPI document. Unrelated untracked test files are excluded.
Keep existing JWT and policy handling
Update snapshots and exact string checks
The checked-in OpenAPI document changed only its information title. The version remains v1.

Mobile action: keep the current API base URL, generated client models, serialization rules, and authentication interceptors. Regenerating a client from this OpenAPI file is optional because the only difference is the displayed API title.
The following endpoints can expose new Ascend wording or visuals. Status codes and payload shapes remain unchanged.
When the provider supplies no first name, a newly created user now receives the fallback first name Ascend instead of Xenoh.
No model change. Do not assume the fallback value is a person's real name.
The not-found message now says that no Ascend account uses the email address.
Display the server message or use localized client copy. Update exact-message tests.
An Organizer-tier rejection now directs the user to Ascend support.
Keep existing error handling. Update exact-message tests and visible fallback copy.
The fallback insight now names Ascend Coach.
No response-shape change. Refresh content snapshots.
The off-topic response now refers to progress inside Ascend in English and Vietnamese.
Treat generated and policy responses as content, not stable identifiers.
The generated PNG now draws A S C E N D in the header and footer instead of the legacy name.
No URL or MIME-type change. Invalidate cached previews if needed.

The fallback-name change affects only new external-login users whose provider data has an empty first name. Existing profiles are not renamed. The API continues to return the existing authentication response contract.

Ascend's shared coaching prompt now identifies the product and coach as Ascend and Ascend Coach. The data contracts remain the same, but generated wording can reflect the new brand. Cached AI content created before deployment may still contain Xenoh until it expires or is regenerated.
Account-wide analysis is framed as an Ascend insight experience.
Plan-progress recommendations inherit the Ascend coaching identity.
Generated tips and the fallback insight use Ascend Coach language.
Coach replies, topic boundaries, and future conversation summaries use Ascend branding.
Cycle-aware recommendations inherit the shared Ascend coaching identity.
Generated starter plans inherit the shared Ascend coaching identity.
AI balance-review language inherits the shared Ascend coaching identity.
Coach-facing AI briefs inherit the shared Ascend coaching identity.
Do not parse AI prose for the Xenoh or Ascend brand name.
Keep rendering the existing typed response fields.
Update golden tests and screenshots that contain legacy generated copy.
If the mobile app caches AI text locally, allow legacy text to age out or clear only the relevant content cache during migration.
POST /api/auth/forgot-password/send-code keeps the same request and response behavior. Its side-effect email now uses Ascend in the subject, plain-text body, HTML header, and reset instructions.
POST /api/auth/account-deletion-requests keeps the same request and response behavior. Its verification email now uses Ascend in the subject and HTML confirmation text.
The default SMTP sender display name changed from Xenoh to Ascend in application settings and SmtpOptions. The configured sender email address is unchanged.

The public PR image endpoint keeps its route, parameters, PNG result, caching behavior, and storage flow. Only the drawn brand lettering changed. Mobile clients that cache the image by URL may continue showing an old stored image until the cache is refreshed or the server generates a new object.
A S C E N D
The following legacy technical identifiers remain active. The mobile app must keep using them until the backend and deployed infrastructure support a coordinated migration.
Keep current base URLs and trusted-host rules.
Keep registered scheme and external-auth callback handling.
Continue sending the existing header names.
No mobile change; backend cookie names remain stable.
Do not rewrite or normalize server payment codes.
No mobile dependency; internal names remain unchanged.

Changing these values as part of a visual rebrand could break social login, analytics attribution, token validation, payment reconciliation, cache separation, or connectivity. Their continued Xenoh naming is intentional compatibility behavior, not incomplete visible branding.
[ ] Keep all current API routes, methods, base URLs, DTOs, and serializers.
[ ] Keep the xenoh mobile callback scheme for social authentication.
[ ] Keep sending X-Xenoh analytics headers exactly as implemented.
[ ] Update client-owned error fallbacks and snapshots from Xenoh to Ascend.
[ ] Do not compare complete AI responses as stable strings.
[ ] Refresh cached PR share images or append an existing cache-busting mechanism after deployment.
[ ] Verify password-reset and account-deletion flows from the mobile app through the received email link or code.
[ ] Test external registration when the provider omits a first name.
[ ] Test Organizer payment-order rejection and competition staff lookup not-found handling.
[ ] Review English and Vietnamese Ascend Coach responses.
[ ] Run a final case-insensitive UI search for Xenoh while allowing documented technical identifiers.
19 before and 19 after; identical path set

The automated checks establish contract stability within the current tracked diff. Mobile release testing should still cover the changed observable flows because email delivery, generated AI text, and image caching depend on runtime services.
